- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for the next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.4), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates prices after a sharp upward spike (e.g., >5% from prior day); add 2–5% buffer to forecast for 3–7 days post-spike.
- Model overestimates early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed; reduce first 5–7 days’ forecast by 1–2%.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to correct; add 0.5–1.5% upward adjustment for next 3–5 days.
- Forecast horizon 1–7 days: model tends to lag true price movements; apply 0.5–1.5% lead adjustment based on sentiment momentum.
- If sentiment turns sharply positive after a negative period, model often misses the rally; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
